correctness.rationale: Every graph edge and every independent triple is reconstructed from the explicit Cartesian-product definition. The verifier enumerates every face below each complementary facet, constructs all vertex-toggle pairs and checks 100% of Hasse cover relations. Hence the matching is acyclic and Forman gives CW wedges; this is a finite exhaustive proof, not sampling.

originality.rationale: The complete seven-case wedge homotopy statement is stronger than and not entailed by the already published integral homology entries in arXiv:2512.04486, Table 4. That work proves only total two-cut homotopy for the circular ladder and explicitly conjectures total three-cut homology. An acyclic matching on the whole face poset adds CW homotopy information. The published infinite Möbius-ladder three-cut result concerns a different graph; no graph isomorphism or homotopy-equivalence reduction is identified. Other primary works do not dominate this finite homotopy statement; unindexed equivalent calculations remain a risk.
residual_risks: The numerical Betti ranks are previously published and have no novelty here.
An unindexed stronger homotopy theorem or alternate discrete-Morse calculation might cover these finite cases.
The finite certificate has not received independent external review; it does not imply an all-n theorem.

value.rationale: The exact k=3 homotopy types for the first seven nonvoid circumferences form a natural contiguous partial classification of the explicitly conjectured circular-ladder family. Published Table 4 provides the numerical homology but not a wedge homotopy type; a complete acyclic Morse certificate upgrades topological information and gives non-shellability. This is a motivated published gap and distinguishes exceptional n=4,5 from the stable n>=6 range within the finite domain. The result is not claimed to extend indefinitely.
